name: FL-19
label: Likely R

key_factors: Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Republican candidate has vastly outraised the Democrat
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 92% Republican
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean and the Republican's overwhelming fundraising advantage make this a heavily favored Republican open seat. Markets price a Republican win near 92%, and no polling or expert ratings suggest movement toward the underfunded Democrat.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending in the district could signal an unexpected shift in this low-information race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this southwest Florida seat to run for governor, creating an open contest in a district that leans Republican by about 14 points. Jim Schwartzel has raised more than $2 million, dwarfing Democrat Victor Arias's roughly $45,000, and prediction markets give the Republican about a 92% chance of holding the seat.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. An open seat removes the incumbent's personal vote edge, but the underlying partisan lean remains firmly favorable to Republicans, keeping this in Likely Republican territory rather than Safe.
